children: China is making progress toward completing a commitment to buy 200 Boeing
aircraft, giving the U.S. aerospace company a potential boost as Washington and Beijing prepare for another round of high-level talks.

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said Monday that about 140 aircraft are in a "good state," while orders for another 10 are being written up. The commitment was announced in May and represented Boeing's first major Chinese aircraft deal in nearly a decade.
The update comes ahead of a meeting this week between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. China has not announced another large Boeing

CEO Kelly Ortberg also has sought to temper expectations that the summit will produce a blockbuster aircraft order. He said last week that he expects additional orders over time, with individual Chinese airlines announcing purchases on their own schedules.
The 200-plane commitment nevertheless could mark the reopening of an important market for Boeing

. Ortberg said in May that a trip to China had achieved the company's key goal of reopening the market for Boeing orders. President Trump said in May that China's purchases eventually could reach as many as 750 aircraft. Boeing at the time characterized the initial 200-plane commitment as the first portion of what could become a larger commercial relationship.

For investors, the latest comments provide more evidence that the 200-aircraft commitment is moving toward firm orders rather than remaining a diplomatic pledge. The bigger question is how quickly those orders translate into deliveries and cash flow. Boeing
already ended the second quarter with a record $715 billion backlog, while production constraints remain a key issue for the company.
China also remains strategically important as Boeing competes with Airbus

for future aircraft demand. Boeing has more than 4,000 737 Max aircraft in its existing backlog, enough to extend production into the 2030s. The Trump-Xi meeting is expected to cover a broader range of economic issues including trade, tariffs, artificial intelligence and critical minerals.

title: China moves closer to finalizing 200-jet Boeing order
